newsitem.title: FRANCE: Controllers strike cuts hundreds of Orly flights.
newsitem.headline: Controllers strike cuts hundreds of Orly flights.

text.p: An air controllers' strike at Paris' Orly airport forced authorities to cancel about half of the estimated 800 daily flights in and out of the French capital's main platform for domestic flights on Wednesday, officials said.
The controllers are on strike to demand parity in bonuses with counterparts at the larger Charles de Gaulle airport at Roissy on the other side of Paris, which mostly handles international flights.
The 120 Orly controllers say they handle about 70 flights an hour, only ten or so less than colleagues at Charles de Gaulle who earn about 1,000 francs ($175) a month more.

The cancellations came as both Air France Europe, the national airline's domestic branch, and Air Liberte and TAT, British Airways-owned French regional airlines, were affected by strikes by pilots or cabin staff.
Their cancelled flights were counted among the estimated 400 flights cancelled at Orly.
